open_points.subject: erasing old audit entries and minting its confirmation id
open_points.text: “the erasure of old entries is the one action whose entry `audit_log` writes itself, inside `erase_audit_entries_before`” but “`operations`” owns “minting the confirmation id only” when the action is accepted
open_points.question: How does `audit_log`, which decides whether the erasure is accepted and writes its entry, obtain the confirmation id from `operations` without minting one for a refused action or depending back on `operations`/`random_values`?
options: `operations` validates first, mints the id, then calls a separately exposed audit-log mutation
`operations` passes a lazy minting capability that `audit_log` invokes only after its checks pass
`operations` mints before calling `erase_audit_entries_before`, consuming an id even if that module refuses the action
open_points.default_guess: Pass a lazy confirmation-id minting capability into `erase_audit_entries_before` and invoke it only after validation succeeds.

witness.initial: The owner has a valid session and confirmation value and submits an audit-erasure date that `audit_log` will refuse, such as a date later than today; the random source is deterministic in a test.
events: `operations` authenticates the owner and consumes the confirmation value.
The owner later performs an accepted confirmed action.
outcomes: An implementation that pre-mints consumes a UUID for the refused erasure, so the later accepted action receives the next UUID.
An implementation that lets `audit_log` request minting only after acceptance consumes no UUID for the refusal, so the later accepted action receives the earlier UUID.
witness.observer: A deterministic test of `random_values`, and any code inspecting the later accepted audit entry, sees the difference.

open_points.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner

open_points.subject: kept and temporary backup filename prefixes
open_points.text: `release_declarations` owns “the kept and temporary backup prefixes, neither beginning with the other,” while `backups` owns “the prefixes and the location rules (rule 5)”
open_points.question: Does `release_declarations` own the prefix values with `backups` only enforcing and using them, or may `backups` define the prefix values itself?
options: `release_declarations` owns the values; `backups` consumes them and owns file handling under them
`backups` owns the values; `release_declarations` merely exposes them
The modules independently define them and startup verifies that they agree
open_points.default_guess: Let `release_declarations` own and expose the values, with `backups` owning only their enforcement and file operations.

witness.initial: A new release changes the declared kept and temporary backup prefixes, while the backup location contains files made under the new prefixes.
events: The instance starts on the new release.
The owner asks for the newest kept backup.
The daily backup run removes temporary files and applies retention.
outcomes: If `backups` consumes the release-owned prefixes, it recognizes the new kept files and cleans the new temporary files.
If `backups` owns an independent prefix choice, it may ignore the release-declared files and operate on a different set of names.
witness.observer: The owner sees a different newest-backup status, and the backup location retains or deletes different files.
